# Catalog

* [Hotfix press parameters](hotfix-press-parameters.md) - Manufacturer and retail heat-fix recipes: Preciosa time-vs-temperature tables by fabric class and side, transfer press settings (160-170 C, 15-25 s, medium pressure), Swarovski range, fabric suitability and correct-bond criteria.
* [Stone and leotard prices](stone-and-leotard-prices.md) - October 2026 retail prices: Swarovski and Preciosa MAXIMA loose stones (about 6 US cents each at ss16), Korean/DMC glass (under 1 cent), rhinestuds, and GK and Snowflake leotard list prices; for the app's price estimate.
* [Stone colour libraries](stone-colour-libraries.md) - Swarovski 2088 colour chart (2018, about 127 entries by family), Preciosa MAXIMA and VIVA hotfix colour subsets, the 2026 Chocolate neutral, and a suggested default WAG palette.
* [Stone coverage density](stone-coverage-density.md) - Stones per square inch, per linear inch and per square centimetre by size (square and hex packing), the area and line rules, and the error in the retail 30ss figure; used for stone-count estimates and price read-outs.
* [Non-round flat-back stone shapes](stone-shapes.md) - Shaped flat-back stones (navette, pear, drop, square, triangle, kite, heart, star and more) with article numbers and the few fixed sizes each comes in, from Swarovski's 2018 catalogue; shaped stones are typically hand-set accents.
* [Stone sizes (ss to millimetres)](stone-sizes.md) - The ss size table with diameters from retail, hobbyist, Swarovski and Preciosa sources, typical use per size, which sizes leotards use (ss6-ss30, ss16/ss20 workhorses) and suggested nominal diameters for the app.

# Design Rule

* [Stone placement rules](stone-placement-rules.md) - Manufacturability checks for stones: keep off seams, elastic and layered areas; hand-set anything above about 5 mm; split layouts into machine-field tiles of up to 6 size/colour hoppers; minimum spacing; fabric restrictions (velvet, foil, mesh). Thresholds ship as adjustable defaults.
* [Relaxed vs stretched stone spacing](stretch-spacing-trap.md) - Stones are rigid and pressed on relaxed (or slightly stretched) flat pieces, so on the body centre-to-centre spacing grows with local fabric stretch while stone size stays fixed; layouts must be previewed and checked in the worn state.

# Domain Concept

* [Crystal brands and grades](crystal-brands-and-grades.md) - Premium Preciosa MAXIMA and Swarovski XIRIUS, then 12-facet stones (VIVA12, LUX, DMC) and 8-11-facet Korean glass; Swarovski left the costume trade in 2021 and one retailer reports reopening in June 2026 (single source).
* [Crystal colour layers, coatings and Aurora Borealis](crystal-coatings-and-ab.md) - Stone colour is three independent layers: glass body colour, back treatment (foil or lacquer) and an optional crown coating such as AB (vapour-deposited thin film on about half the crown), AB 2X, Shimmer or metallic effects.
* [Crystal count as tier and price signal](crystal-counts-and-tiers.md) - Crystal count is the clearest measure of a leotard's tier: US Olympic leotards went from 184 crystals (2008) to 6,359-10,000+ (2024); club leotards are sold in tiers of about 20, 640, 1,150 and 1,775+ crystals; proposed tier vocabulary for the app's count budget.
* [Embellishments on WAG competition leotards](embellishments-on-wag-leotards.md) - Overview: competition leotards carry heat-applied flat-back crystals first, hole-less spangles second, plus nailheads, pearls, appliqué and embroidery; trade vocabulary and the object types the app should model.
* [Flat-back crystal anatomy](flat-back-crystal-anatomy.md) - A hotfix crystal is a faceted glass crown (table plus 8-18 facets, no pavilion) over a mirror foil and a heat-activated glue layer; glass index about 1.5-1.8; height roughly 0.4 x diameter.
* [Pearls, nailheads, appliqué, embroidery and print embellishments](other-embellishments.md) - Beyond crystals and spangles: aluminium rhinestuds/nailheads, hand-placed hotfix pearls (first on US Olympic leotards in 2024), laser-cut appliqué glued then stitched, embroidered logos, sublimation and foil/glitter surfaces.
* [Stone placement vocabulary](placement-vocabulary.md) - The small set of moves leotard designers use with stones: outline, lettering/logo fill, region fill, gradient scatter (cascade, rainfall, meteor shower), clusters, bursts, stripes/chevrons, swirls, alternation and accent stones, plus size-mix and colour rules of thumb.
* [Rhinestone layout software baseline](rhinestone-layout-software.md) - Existing rhinestone tools (Sierra Hotfix Era, TRW Design Wizard, Silhouette Studio, Inkscape/Ink-Stitch) are 2D and built for flat transfers; their verified features (path and area fills, mixed sizes, overlap marking, single-stone edit, pricing, machine export) are the baseline a 3D leotard tool must match.
* [Spangles and sequins](spangles-and-sequins.md) - On leotards a spangle is a hole-less 2-6 mm plastic disc punched from a reel onto transfer tape and heat-pressed; holographic, metallic, matte or glossy; used for team names and logos. Sewn sequins are a dance/costume technique.

# Open Question

* [Embellishment data gaps](embellishment-data-gaps.md) (draft) - What the embellishment research could not establish: stone geometry and optical constants, GK's grade and spangle definitions, maker stone sizes and spacing rules, stretch durability, machine formats, competitor tools and conflicting facet counts; with how to close each.

# Process

* [Heat-fix crystal production process](heat-fix-production-process.md) - How leotard stones are applied industrially: CAD layout, setting machine (6 hoppers, about 170-600 stones/min, 2-5 mm stones, 400 x 400 mm field) onto transfer film, heat press on flat pieces, hand-set large stones and pearls, then seaming; plus template and hand methods.
